title: On friendship
hook: a friend is a person with whom I may be sincere (Friendship, 1841)

segments.voice: Yesterday, nothing great without enthusiasm: the line near the end of Emerson's Circles. Your line was with enthusiasm. What small thing got the whole of you? Day one thousand two hundred three.

Scroll the contacts on a phone. Plenty of names. A coworker. The plumber. Someone from a wedding. A parent from school pickup. Old classmates who might not recognize the voice anymore. Now a harder question, the kind that slows the scrolling down: which of these names could hear a true thing from you, the unpolished version, the thing you haven't tidied up yet? Emerson asked something like that in his essay Friendship, and his answer is short enough to fit on a sticky note on the fridge. Today, his test for a friend.
screen: `PLENTY OF NAMES.` → `WHO GETS THE UNPOLISHED VERSION?` → `A TEST FOR A FRIEND.`

segments.voice: First, the test itself. Emerson writes: "A friend is a person with whom I may be sincere. Before him I may think aloud." Think aloud. Not a finished speech, not the best version. The half-formed thought, the doubt, the thing you're not sure you believe yet. With most people we edit before we speak. With a friend, Emerson says, the editing can stop. Second, what a friendship is made of. In the same essay he names two elements. One is truth. The other is tenderness. Truth alone can turn into a person who tells you every flaw and calls it honesty. Tenderness alone can turn into a person who only tells you what you want to hear. A friend, in Emerson's picture, holds both at once. Third, the way in. Emerson turns the question around: "The only way to have a friend is to be one." So the test runs both directions. Who can I be sincere with? And who can be sincere with me, because I've shown I can hear it without punishing them for it? Fourth, what sincere is not. It isn't blurting. It isn't using honesty as a weapon. Emerson's sincere friend is the one with whom the masks can come off because it's safe to take them off. That kind of safety gets built slowly, by small true things said gently, and small true things received well. Even one friend like that is a great deal.
screen: `A PERSON WITH WHOM I MAY BE SINCERE.` · `TRUTH AND TENDERNESS.` · `THE ONLY WAY TO HAVE A FRIEND.` · `SINCERE IS NOT HARSH.` · then, large: `BEFORE HIM I MAY THINK ALOUD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: get ready to be sincere with one friend. Settle, and breathe. Let one friend's face come to mind. Turn Emerson's test around: is this a person who can think aloud in front of you? Remember the last time they told you something unpolished. How did you take it? Then ask what you could do so they'd feel safe enough to do it again. A question asked and then left room for. A pause before advice. A half-formed thought of your own, offered first. Pick one. The bell holds the time.
On friendship. Emerson's essay, with its plain test: a friend is a person with whom I may be sincere, made of truth and tenderness together. Today's word.
Your line: sincere. Today, with the friend you pictured, try the one thing you picked, and let one of you think aloud. Day one thousand two hundred three.

howItsDone: Readers of Emerson's Friendship often hold onto its two elements, truth and tenderness, as a way of judging and deepening their closest friendships.

fork.setup: a close friend asks how you're really doing. it's been a hard week and you haven't told anyone. what does Emerson's test point toward?
options: the true answer, said plainly and kindly.
turn the question back to them.
fork.reveal: Emerson: "a friend is a person with whom I may be sincere. before him I may think aloud." a friend is exactly where the polished answer can be set down.

trapdoor: what you thought: a friend is someone you like being around.
what it means: a friend is someone with whom the editing can stop, and you can think aloud.
what a scholar hears: Emerson's essay builds friendship from two elements, truth and tenderness, and turns the question back on the reader: the only way to have a friend is to be one.
